problem: Model-free RL agents for object-goal visual navigation lack a forward model that tells them the consequences of their actions, which hurts robustness and efficiency, especially without an object detector.
motivation: Object-goal navigation with model-free RL achieves strong results but has no explicit notion of what a successful future looks like. Giving the agent an imagined successful future latent state could guide better action selection and improve success and efficiency.
key_idea: Train a forward model that, from the start of an episode, predicts the latent representation of a future state that would lead to success, and use this imagined success state to condition the model-free RL policy, with a replay buffer alternating policy and forward-model training.
insight: Explicitly imagining a success-leading latent future state gives the policy a goal-like signal that improves robustness, most visibly when no object detector is available (about 5% absolute SR gain). With an off-the-shelf detector the gain is smaller (about 3% SR, 2% SPL). Only the abstract was available, so no ablation details can be cited.
method: Forward model (success imagination): predicts a latent representation of a future state, from the start of the episode, as it would be if the episode were successful.
Model-free RL policy: the base object-goal navigation RL agent, augmented with the imagined success latent state to choose actions.
Replay buffer integration: a replay buffer is added to the model-free RL, and training alternates between updating the policy and the forward model for efficient training.
Optional object detector: an off-the-shelf detector is combined with the agent to better distinguish the target object.

setting.backbone: model-free RL policy with a learned latent forward model (details not given in abstract)
setting.training_data: trained by RL in simulation on object-goal navigation episodes with a replay buffer (scale not stated in abstract)
setting.observation: egocentric visual observations (RGB) and target object; not detailed in abstract

results: Without an object detector, ForeSI gives about 5% absolute SR improvement over the model-free RL baselines. With an off-the-shelf detector it gives about 3% absolute SR and about 2% absolute SPL improvement.
